title: Jump Game
statement: nums[i] is the maximum jump length from index i. Starting at index 0, return True if you can reach the last index.

hints.1_question: You don't need the exact path, only whether the last index can be reached. What single number summarises everything reachable so far?
hints.2_nudge: Keep the farthest index reachable. If you ever stand on an index beyond it, you are stuck.
hints.3_big_hint: far = 0; for i, x: if i > far: return False; far = max(far, i + x). Return True.

known_bugs.name: any zero means failure
known_bugs.code:
def canJump(nums):
    return 0 not in nums[:-1] if len(nums) > 1 else True
known_bugs.followup: In [2, 0, 0] you can jump over the zeros. Does the presence of a zero always block you?

known_bugs.name: always jumps the full length
known_bugs.followup: In [2, 5, 0, 0] is it right to jump the full 2 from index 0, or would a shorter jump be better?

known_bugs.name: farthest reach computed one short
known_bugs.followup: From index i with value x, which index is the farthest you can land on - i + x or i + x - 1?

followups: Why is tracking only the farthest reach enough?
How would you recover an actual path of jumps?
